uncited: **Redundancy Exploitation:** The core principle is to identify and eliminate redundancy in the volumetric data.
**Transformation/Encoding:** Data is transformed into a domain where redundancy is more apparent or compact.
**Quantization (Lossy):** For lossy compression, continuous or high-precision values are mapped to a discrete set of representatives.
ZFP (Zstandard Floating-Point) is a floating-point compression algorithm using fixed-rate compression, encoding blocks of 4x4x4 floating-point values.

The algorithm converts block values to a common fixed-point format by factoring out the largest exponent of floating-point values within each block, then converts resulting normalized values to a two's complement fixed-point format.
Blocks are then spatially decorrelated by converting to a different basis based on a tensor product transformation (e.g., DWT, DCT).
A key pitfall is that decompression is only efficient when using caches.
It quantizes wavelet coefficients (concentrated around zero) into 2 or 3 bits using non-uniform quantization.
Data is stored as linear arrays per level.
Each entry has a leading mask defining which coefficients were removed, followed by the coefficients themselves.
Westermann's method uses masks and offsets for speed, introducing memory overhead.
In G-PROG mode, the set of quantizers is applied to the whole set of subband images before passing to the next subband.
The scanning order follows the decomposition level: all subbands at level $l$ are scanned before passing to level $l+1$.
Quantisation PSNR loss vs original is at most −0.679 dB (median −0.012 dB).
Quantised render PSNR vs float32 render is 59–88 dB.
Shipped rule storage is 9.63 bytes/splat (10.09 bytes/splat if re-chunked to 64 KiB without prefilter, 14.3% below uniform Blosc-zstd level-3 bit-shuffle baseline).
During BTC, the data is decomposed into equal-sized blocks.
Luminance Y is used to identify the model structure.
The model $m$ is losslessly and independently coded.
Value compression in volume rendering has evolved from simple scalar quantization to complex transform-based and hardware-accelerated methods.
